With the investigator torso facing the capture view, the photograph is in her anatomical left hand at image-right and the pen is in her anatomical right hand at image-left. Both hands connect through their own visible wrists/cuffs; the pointing hand belongs to the attendant.

The held fountain-pen nib projects above the notebook with a visible separated shadow/air relation in pen-tip-native-crop.png; its nib makes no continuous ink stroke into the page at the shutter. The writing hand rests in a paused grip.

The attendant index fingertip meets the square terminal landing at the outer end of a narrow pier extending from the mapped shoreline into blue water. The pier neck and terminal outline are visible together, rather than a nearby route fork.

The eyes are visibly lowered toward the counter rather than the attendant face, but the pupil/eye orientation in gaze-crop.png does not resolve a unique line to the fingertip on the distant terminal landing. Looking down generally is insufficient for the unchanged exact same-target criterion.
A ticket-booth counter, empty boarding walkway and water/landing are visible at dusk. A closure notice supports the end-of-service impression; no claim about an actual ferry schedule is inferred.

The investigator retains a dark jaw-length bob with separated wispy fringe, rounded/soft facial outline, large dark eyes, fine brows and soft lips consistent with the supplied appearance. This is visible appearance continuity only.
